summary: Opala territory (Tshopo province), south-west of Kisangani along the Lomami river, is far from the eastern conflict zones and no armed group is known to hold territory there. The state administers Opala town and the Yaleko secteur; the Congolese National Police (PNC) is the main day-to-day security force, with limited FARDC presence. Local land, chieftaincy and intercommunal disputes occur in Tshopo but are not known to have produced lasting non-state control in Opala. Web research was unavailable for this run, so confidence is medium for Opala town and low for rural villages.

zones.description: Opala town (territory seat on the Lomami: Centre Commercial, Busoko Bas)
zones.evidence: Territorial headquarters with state administration, PNC commissariat and courts; no reports of armed-group activity in the town. No web sources could be retrieved in this run (search budget exhausted, search engines and Wikipedia blocked), so the assessment rests on the absence of known armed-group activity in Opala territory.

zones.description: Yaleko secteur villages (Yaleko and Yakusu health zones, Kisangani-Opala road axis)
zones.evidence: Rural Mbole villages north of Opala toward Kisangani with no known armed-group presence; order assumed kept by PNC posts and customary authorities under state administration. No web sources could be retrieved in this run (search budget exhausted, search engines and Wikipedia blocked), so the assessment rests on the absence of known armed-group activity in Opala territory.

zones.description: Rural Opala secteur villages (Opala and Ikela health zones, west/south-west of Opala town toward Tshuapa)
zones.evidence: Remote forest villages with no known armed-group presence; state presence is thin but no non-state actor is reported to exercise control.
